rows.title: Wall Sina, Goodbye: Part 1
rows.note: Shipped as the DVD bundled with the LIMITED EDITION of Attack on Titan manga vol 24 (『ＤＶＤ付き 進撃の巨人（２４）限定版』, ISBN 978-4-06-397047-0). Kodansha's own product page prints 発売日 2017年12月08日 and 「Wall Sina, Goodbye（アニ外伝）」をWIT STUDIOが前後編で完全アニメ化！／※本限定版には前編を収録しています。 Franchise OAD ordinal #16.5A (the fandom's OVA 6; Crunchyroll's 'Attack on Titan OADs' Episode 6). Official English on Crunchyroll/Funimation: 'Lost Girls: Wall Sina, Goodbye: Part 1'.

rows.title: Wall Sina, Goodbye: Part 2
rows.note: DVD bundled with the LIMITED EDITION of manga vol 25 (ISBN 978-4-06-397048-7); Kodansha's page prints 発売日 2018年04月09日 and 「進撃の巨人」のスピンオフ小説「ＬＯＳＴ ＧＩＲＬＳ」をアニメーション化 (that page does not itself say 後編 — ja-WP's OAD table, the licensor's OAD Archive listing and dアニメストア's two-episode work page all place 後編 on vol 25). Franchise OAD ordinal #16.5B (OVA 7; Crunchyroll Episode 7). Official English: 'Lost Girls: Wall Sina, Goodbye: Part 2'.

rows.title: Lost in the Cruel World
rows.note: DVD bundled with the LIMITED EDITION of manga vol 26 (ISBN 978-4-06-397049-4); Kodansha's page prints 発売日 2018年08月09日 and 「Lost in the cruel world（ミカサ外伝）」をWIT STUDIOが完全アニメ化! This OAD has NO franchise number at all — shingeki.tv and aot-portal.com both list it as '#???' (the fandom cites the title card for the same). Official English: 'Lost Girls: Lost in the Cruel World'.

numbering_basis: Release order of THIS entry's three OADs, 1-3 (2017-12-08 → 2018-04-09 → 2018-08-09). No Japanese source numbers the run itself: the licensor's own OAD Archive listing (shingeki.tv 商品情報 and the official portal aot-portal.com) and dアニメストア label them with the FRANCHISE OVA ordinal #16.5A / #16.5B / #??? — the third has no number, its title card reads '???'. The Attack on Titan Wiki calls them OVA 6 / 7 / 8 and Crunchyroll's 'Attack on Titan OADs' collection numbers them Episodes 6 / 7 / 8. en-WP's 'Attack on Titan: Lost Girls' episode table prints 16.5A / 16.5B / ??? in its EpisodeNumber column but carries 1 / 2 / 3 in EpisodeNumber2 — that release-order column is the one that matches our numbering. Dates are the first Japanese release of each row = the manga limited edition's ship date (the disc bundle), per the protocol.

flags_for_sean: en-WP DATE DEFECT on row 1 — do NOT seed from its table cell. The Episodes table prints OriginalAirDate = December 9, 2017 for 16.5A, while the SAME article's lead prose and its OAD infobox both say December 8, 2017. Kodansha's own vol-24 限定版 product page prints 発売日 2017年12月08日, ja-WP's OAD table and tankōbon table both say 2017年12月8日, and the fandom says December 8. The grid carries 2017-12-08.

NUMBERING TRAP CONFIRMED AND WIDER THAN THE ASK. It is not only en-WP: every Japanese licensor page uses the franchise OAD ordinal (#16.5A / #16.5B / #???), the fandom uses OVA 6/7/8, and Crunchyroll's 'Attack on Titan OADs' collection uses Episodes 6/7/8. The THIRD OAD has no number in any official space — shingeki.tv and aot-portal.com print literally '#???' and the fandom sources that to the title card. Our 1-3 is release order; the only source that prints it is en-WP's secondary EpisodeNumber2 column. Never store 16.5A / 6 / ??? as a row number.

TITLE RENDERING FORK (cosmetic, but pick one convention). Japanese: the two licensor pages I read directly (shingeki.tv OAD Archive, aot-portal.com) print 'Wall Sina,Goodbye―前編―' with no space after the comma and none before the dashes; dアニメストア and the official niconico OAD channel print 'Wall Sina,Goodbye ―前編―'; ja-WP puts a line break there; Kodansha's prose writes 'Wall Sina, Goodbye（アニ外伝）' with the comma space. The grid uses the spaced dash form. Row 3's Japanese title is Latin-script lowercase on every licensor page ('Lost in the cruel world'); only the official ENGLISH title capitalizes it.

ENGLISH TITLE PREFIX STRIPPED. Crunchyroll and Funimation print 'Lost Girls: Wall Sina, Goodbye: Part 1' / 'Part 2' / 'Lost Girls: Lost in the Cruel World' — and the Japanese licensor does the same on the disc listing ('Lost girls Wall Sina,Goodbye（前編）'). The 'Lost Girls' prefix is this series' own name, so it is stripped in `title`. Licensor form is 'Part 1' / 'Part 2'; en-WP and the fandom use 'Part One' / 'Part Two' — say the word if you want the spelled-out form.
COUNT OK: 3 rows = AniList 99634's 3 episodes. No mismatch, no bonus disc, no recap.

NOT THE GRID DATES, recorded so they are not mistaken for one later: all eight OADs were later collected on the 進撃の巨人 OAD Archive Blu-ray (PCXG-50788, Pony Canyon, 2022-04-27); shingeki.tv's announcement says the three LOST GIRLS/悔いなき選択 OADs had been broadcast on NHK (the fandom dates the 'Lost in the cruel world' NHK 総合 airing 2021-11-28, as an extra of the Special Omnibus); the English releases were 2021-12-19 subtitled and 2022-06-12 / 06-19 / 06-26 dubbed. The grid carries the FIRST Japanese release = the limited-edition disc ship date.

CONTENT NOTE for the later standing programme, NOT a grid claim: Seko's source novel holds THREE stories — 'Lost in the cruel world', 'Wall Sina, Goodbye' and 'Lost Girls' — and the third, 'Lost Girls', was never animated. The fandom (cross-check) says rows 1-2 adapt vol 1 of Ryōsuke Fuji's Bessatsu Shōnen Magazine manga of the novel (chapters Carly Stratmann / Wayne Eisner / Wald and Lou / Coderoin / Annie Leonhart) and row 3 adapts vol 2 (Eren Yeager / Shiganshina / Airplane / Mirror Man). Note the source chain for the typing sitting: visual novel (2013, Nitroplus) → novel (2014) → manga (2015-16) → OAD (2017-18); the anime's chapter space, if any is ever mapped, is the 2-volume Lost Girls manga's own, not Isayama's 1-139.
